summary.en: The northernmost and largest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, spanning Manchuria and the northern peninsula. It repelled Sui and Tang invasions before falling to a Tang–Silla alliance in 668. Capitals: Jolbon, Gungnae (Ji'an), then Pyongyang from 427.
summary.zh: 朝鲜三国中最北、疆域最大的国家，地跨中国东北与朝鲜半岛北部。曾击退隋、唐的进攻，668年被唐与新罗联军所灭。都城先后为卒本、国内城（今集安），427年起迁至平壤。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Goguryeo
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Goguryeo

note: The 37 BCE founding date is traditional (Samguk sagi).

summary.en: Kingdom of southwestern Korea that transmitted Buddhism, writing and craftsmen to Japan. Driven south from the Han River by Goguryeo in 475, it ruled from Ungjin and then Sabi until conquered by Tang and Silla in 660.
summary.zh: 朝鲜半岛西南部的王国，曾向日本传入佛教、文字与工匠。475年被高句丽逐出汉江流域后，先后以熊津、泗沘为都，660年被唐与新罗联军所灭。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Baekje
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Baekje Historic Areas
Wikipedia: Paekche

note: The 18 BCE founding date and early reigns are traditional.

summary.en: Kingdom of southeastern Korea that allied with Tang to conquer Baekje and Goguryeo, then expelled Tang to rule most of the peninsula as Unified Silla from 668/676. It declined in the 9th century and surrendered to Goryeo in 935.
summary.zh: 朝鲜半岛东南部的王国，联合唐朝灭百济、高句丽后又驱逐唐军，自668/676年起以“统一新罗”统治半岛大部。9世纪走向衰落，935年归降高丽。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Silla
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Silla

note: The 57 BCE founding is traditional. Wikidata ends Silla in 892 (start of the Later Three Kingdoms); the formal end was its surrender to Goryeo in 935.

summary.en: A league of small iron-producing polities in the Nakdong River basin, closely linked by trade to the Wa of Japan. Its members were absorbed by Silla, the last, Daegaya, in 562.
summary.zh: 洛东江流域盛产铁器的小国联盟，与日本的倭国贸易往来密切。其成员先后被新罗吞并，最后的大伽倻于562年灭亡。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gaya confederacy
Iryeon, Samguk yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, c. 1281)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Kaya confederacy

note: The AD 42 founding and King Suro's reign follow the legendary Garakguk-gi preserved in the Samguk yusa.

summary.en: A kingdom founded by Dae Jo-yeong, a former Goguryeo general, ruling Manchuria and northern Korea with Goguryeo and Mohe populations. Known to Tang as "the flourishing land in the East", it was destroyed by the Khitan Liao in 926.
summary.zh: 由原高句丽将领大祚荣建立的王国，统治中国东北与朝鲜半岛北部，居民包括高句丽人与靺鞨人。被唐朝誉为“海东盛国”，926年为契丹辽朝所灭。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Balhae
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Parhae

note: Its ethnic composition and historical affiliation are debated between Korean and Chinese historiography.

summary.en: The dynasty from which the name "Korea" derives. Goryeo reunified the peninsula in 936, fostered Buddhism, celadon and printing, endured Khitan and Mongol invasions and became a Yuan vassal before being replaced by Joseon.
summary.zh: “Korea”一名即源于高丽。高丽于936年统一半岛，崇奉佛教，青瓷与印刷术发达，历经契丹、蒙古入侵并一度成为元朝藩属，最终被朝鲜王朝取代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Goryeo
Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Goryeo

summary.en: Korea's last dynasty, founded by Yi Seong-gye and ruling for five centuries. A Neo-Confucian state with a literati bureaucracy, it created Hangul, survived the Japanese and Manchu invasions, and was opened by unequal treaties before becoming the Korean Empire in 1897.
summary.zh: 由李成桂建立，是朝鲜半岛最后一个王朝，延续五百余年。以性理学立国、实行两班文官统治，创制了训民正音，历经壬辰战争与丙子之役，近代被迫签订不平等条约，1897年改称大韩帝国。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Joseon
Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Joseon

summary.en: King Gojong proclaimed himself emperor in 1897 to assert Korea's independence from Qing China. Despite modernising reforms, the empire became a Japanese protectorate in 1905 and was annexed in 1910.
summary.zh: 1897年高宗称帝，宣示朝鲜脱离清朝而独立。尽管推行了光武改革，大韩帝国仍于1905年沦为日本保护国，1910年被日本吞并。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Korean Empire

name.zh: 日本殖民统治时期的朝鲜

summary.en: Korea was governed as the colony of Chōsen by a Japanese Governor-General from 1910 until Japan's defeat in 1945. The period saw industrial development for Japanese ends, forced assimilation policies and wartime labour mobilisation.
summary.zh: 1910年至1945年日本战败期间，朝鲜作为日本殖民地“朝鲜”由朝鲜总督统治。这一时期出现了服务于日本的工业开发、强制同化政策与战时劳动力征用。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Korea under Japanese rule
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Wikipedia: Korea under Japanese rule

summary.en: The era in which the Yamato court in the Nara basin, at first a paramount chieftaincy that built great keyhole tombs, consolidated rule over much of Japan, adopted Buddhism and Chinese-style law, and began calling its ruler tennō.
summary.zh: 以奈良盆地为中心的大和政权时期。大和起初为修筑巨大前方后圆坟的豪族联盟首领，后逐步统一日本大部，接受佛教与中国式律令制度，并开始以“天皇”称呼君主。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Yamato period

note: Start date (c. 250, the beginning of the Kofun period) is approximate; reign dates before the 6th century are traditional.

summary.en: The ritsuryō state at its height, governed from Heijō-kyō under Chinese-style codes. The period produced the Kojiki, Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū and state-sponsored Buddhism centred on Tōdai-ji.
summary.zh: 律令国家的鼎盛时期，以平城京为中心依照中国式律令治国。这一时期编成了《古事记》《日本书纪》和《万叶集》，并形成以东大寺为中心的国家佛教。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nara-period Japan
Shoku Nihongi (797)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Nara period

note: The court left Nara in 784 for Nagaoka-kyō; the period is conventionally closed in 794.

summary.en: Four centuries in which the court at Heian-kyō, dominated by Fujiwara regents and later by retired emperors, produced a refined aristocratic culture and kana literature, while provincial warrior bands grew in power.
summary.zh: 以平安京为中心的约四百年。朝廷先由藤原氏摄关、后由退位上皇（院政）主导，孕育出精致的贵族文化与假名文学，同时地方武士集团日益壮大。

name.zh: 后白河天皇（天皇及上皇）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Heian-period Japan
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 2: Heian Japan (1999)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Heian period

summary.en: Japan's first warrior government, founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo and later run by the Hōjō regents. It repelled the Mongol invasions but was overthrown in 1333 by Emperor Go-Daigo's supporters.
summary.zh: 日本第一个武家政权，由源赖朝创建，后由北条氏执权掌控。它击退了蒙古入侵，1333年被后醍醐天皇一方推翻。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kamakura shogunate
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Wikipedia: Kamakura shogunate

note: Start dates of 1180, 1185 and 1192 are all used; Wikidata gives 1200.

summary.en: The shogunate of the Ashikaga family, based in Kyoto's Muromachi district. It flourished under Yoshimitsu, who reunited the rival courts and traded with Ming China, but lost real power after the Ōnin War; Oda Nobunaga ended it in 1573.
summary.zh: 足利氏的幕府，设于京都室町。足利义满时期最为鼎盛，统一南北朝并与明朝开展勘合贸易；应仁之乱后实权丧失，1573年被织田信长终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Muromachi (Ashikaga) shogunate
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Ashikaga shogunate

summary.en: The military government founded by Tokugawa Ieyasu that gave Japan some 250 years of peace through a balance between the shogun and some 260 domains, strict status order and controlled foreign relations, until it returned power to the emperor in 1867.
summary.zh: 德川家康建立的武家政权，通过将军与约二百六十个藩的平衡、严格的身份秩序以及受控的对外关系，使日本维持了约二百五十年的和平，1867年大政奉还天皇。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tokugawa shogunate
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Tokugawa shogunate

summary.en: The modern imperial state created by the Meiji Restoration. It industrialised rapidly, won wars against China (1895) and Russia (1905), colonised Taiwan and Korea, and expanded across Asia until its defeat in 1945; the 1947 constitution replaced it.
summary.zh: 明治维新后建立的近代帝国。它迅速实现工业化，先后战胜清朝（1895年）与俄国（1905年），殖民台湾与朝鲜，并在亚洲各地扩张，1945年战败，1947年新宪法施行后终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Empire of Japan
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Wikipedia: Empire of Japan

note: Hirohito reigned until 1989; his entry is truncated at the 1947 end of the Empire.

capital.zh: 邪马台（位置有争议，图示为缠向说）

summary.en: The leading polity of the Wa described in the Chinese Wei zhi, ruled by the shaman-queen Himiko and then by Iyo. Whether it lay in the Nara basin or northern Kyushu is one of the oldest debates in Japanese history.
summary.zh: 中国《魏志》所记载的倭人诸国之首，先后由女王卑弥呼和壹与统治。它究竟位于奈良盆地还是九州北部，是日本史上最古老的争论之一。

sources.title: Chen Shou, Sanguozhi, Wei shu 30: Account of the Wa
J. Edward Kidder, Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai (2007)
Wikipedia: Yamatai

note: Dates are inferred from Chinese records (unrest c. 180s; last embassy 266). Wikidata uses a broad 100–300.

summary.en: Founded by the Silla general Gyeon Hwon in the southwest, claiming the heritage of Baekje. It sacked Gyeongju in 927 but was torn apart when Gyeon Hwon's son deposed him; Gyeon Hwon fled to Goryeo, which destroyed his kingdom in 936.
summary.zh: 由新罗将领甄萱在西南部建立，自称继承百济。927年曾攻破庆州，但甄萱被其子废黜后国家分裂；甄萱投奔高丽，936年后百济被高丽所灭。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Later Baekje

note: Gyeon Hwon rebelled in 892 and proclaimed the kingdom at Wansanju in 900.

summary.en: Founded by the renegade monk Gung Ye as Later Goguryeo in 901 and renamed Majin and then Taebong. Gung Ye's growing tyranny, including claims to be the Maitreya Buddha, led his generals to overthrow him in 918 in favour of Wang Geon, who founded Goryeo.
summary.zh: 由出家人弓裔于901年建立，初称后高句丽，后改称摩震、泰封。弓裔日益暴虐，甚至自称弥勒佛，918年其部将推翻他，拥立王建建立高丽。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Taebong

summary.en: The central of the three kingdoms (Sanzan) of 14th-century Okinawa. King Satto opened tribute relations with Ming China in 1372; Shō Hashi seized the throne for his family in 1406 and used Chūzan to unify the island.
summary.zh: 14世纪冲绳三山中位于中部的王国。察度王于1372年与明朝建立朝贡关系；1406年尚巴志为其家族夺取王位，并以中山为基础统一全岛。

sources.title: Ming shilu (Veritable Records of the Ming), Hongwu 5 (1372)
George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)
Wikipedia: Chūzan

note: The start date 1314 follows the traditional Sanzan chronology.

summary.en: A maritime kingdom centred on Okinawa that traded between China, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia as a tributary of the Ming and Qing. Conquered by Satsuma in 1609, it kept its court and Chinese ties until Japan annexed it as Okinawa Prefecture in 1879.
summary.zh: 以冲绳为中心的海洋王国，作为明清两朝的朝贡国，在中国、日本、朝鲜和东南亚之间开展贸易。1609年被萨摩征服后仍保留王廷和对华关系，1879年被日本吞并为冲绳县。

sources.title: George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)
Gregory Smits, Visions of Ryukyu: Identity and Ideology in Early-Modern Thought and Politics (University of Hawaii Press, 1999)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ryukyu Islands
Wikipedia: Ryukyu Kingdom

note: The First Shō dynasty ended in 1469; Shō En founded the Second Shō dynasty, which ruled until 1879.

name.zh: 织丰政权（安土桃山时代）

summary.en: The age of the great unifiers, from Oda Nobunaga's entry into Kyoto in 1568 through Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of all Japan by 1590, to Tokugawa Ieyasu's appointment as shogun in 1603. It is named after Nobunaga's Azuchi Castle and Hideyoshi's Fushimi (Momoyama) Castle.
summary.zh: 统一者的时代：从1568年织田信长进入京都，经丰臣秀吉于1590年统一全国，到1603年德川家康就任征夷大将军为止。时代名称来自信长的安土城和秀吉的伏见（桃山）城。

name.zh: 德川家康（关原之战后实际掌权）

sources.title: Mary Elizabeth Berry, Hideyoshi (Harvard University Press, 1982)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Azuchi-Momoyama period
Wikipedia: Azuchi–Momoyama period

note: Some historians end the period in 1600 (Sekigahara); 1603 is used here so the band joins the Tokugawa shogunate.

summary.en: The Matsumae (formerly Kakizaki) house held a shogunal monopoly on trade with the Ainu from 1604, ruling the Wajin enclave in southern Ezo without rice lands. The shogunate took Ezo under direct rule in 1807–21 and again from 1855 amid fear of Russia; the domain was abolished in 1871.
summary.zh: 松前氏（原蛎崎氏）自1604年起获得幕府授予的对阿伊努贸易垄断权，统治虾夷地南部的和人地区，领内没有稻田。由于担忧俄国，幕府于1807至1821年及1855年后两度直接管辖虾夷地；1871年废藩。

sources.title: Brett L. Walker, The Conquest of Ainu Lands: Ecology and Culture in Japanese Expansion, 1590–1800 (University of California Press, 2001)
David L. Howell, Capitalism from Within: Economy, Society, and the State in a Japanese Fishery (University of California Press, 1995)
Wikipedia: Matsumae Domain

note: Yoshihiro led the house from 1590; 1604 is the date of the Tokugawa trade charter.

summary.en: American-led occupation under the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers. It demilitarised Japan, held war-crimes trials, carried out land reform, broke up the zaibatsu, enfranchised women and introduced the 1947 constitution, then shifted toward economic recovery as the Cold War began. It ended with the San Francisco treaty in 1952.
summary.zh: 由美国主导、在盟军最高司令官统辖下进行的占领。占领当局解除日本武装，审判战犯，实行土地改革，解散财阀，赋予女性选举权，并推动1947年宪法的制定；冷战开始后转向经济复兴。1952年《旧金山和约》生效后结束。

name.zh: 道格拉斯·麦克阿瑟（盟军最高司令官）
马修·李奇微（盟军最高司令官）

sources.title: John W. Dower, Embracing Defeat: Japan in the Wake of World War II (Norton, 1999)
Takemae Eiji, Inside GHQ: The Allied Occupation of Japan and Its Legacy (Continuum, 2002)
Wikipedia: Occupation of Japan

note: Yoshida was also prime minister in 1946–47.

summary.en: The State of Japan under the 1947 constitution: a parliamentary democracy with the emperor as symbol, dominated for most of its history by the Liberal Democratic Party, allied to the United States, and from the 1960s one of the world's largest economies.
summary.zh: 1947年宪法下的日本国：以天皇为象征的议会民主制国家，大部分时间由自由民主党执政，与美国结盟，自1960年代起跻身世界最大经济体之列。

sources.title: Andrew Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)
Prime Minister of Japan and His Cabinet: Successive Prime Ministers
Wikipedia: Japan

note: Rulers listed are notable prime ministers; Abe also served in 2006–07.

name.en: US Army Military Government in Korea
name.zh: 驻朝鲜美国陆军司令部军政厅

summary.en: The American administration of Korea south of the 38th parallel from September 1945 until the Republic of Korea was proclaimed in August 1948. It kept much of the colonial bureaucracy and police, suppressed leftist people's committees and organised the UN-supervised elections of May 1948.
summary.zh: 1945年9月至1948年8月大韩民国成立期间，美国对三八线以南朝鲜的管理机构。它保留了大量殖民时期的官僚和警察，压制左翼人民委员会，并组织了1948年5月联合国监督下的选举。

name.zh: 阿奇博尔德·阿诺德（军政长官）

sources.title: Bruce Cumings, The Origins of the Korean War, vol. 1 (1981)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Migunjeong (US military government)
Wikipedia: United States Army Military Government in Korea

summary.en: The Soviet occupation authority north of the 38th parallel. It worked through Korean people's committees, from February 1946 the Provisional People's Committee chaired by Kim Il-sung, which carried out land reform and nationalised industry before the DPRK was proclaimed in September 1948.
summary.zh: 三八线以北的苏联占领当局。它通过朝鲜人民委员会实施统治，1946年2月起由金日成任委员长的北朝鲜临时人民委员会推行土地改革和工业国有化，直到1948年9月朝鲜民主主义人民共和国成立。

name.zh: 伊万·奇斯佳科夫（第25集团军司令）
金日成（人民委员会委员长）

sources.title: Charles K. Armstrong, The North Korean Revolution, 1945–1950 (Cornell University Press, 2003)
Andrei Lankov, From Stalin to Kim Il Sung: The Formation of North Korea, 1945–1960 (Rutgers, 2002)
Wikipedia: Soviet Civil Administration

note: Soviet authority formally passed to Korean committees in 1946–47, but Soviet troops and advisers remained until late 1948.

summary.en: Founded in the south on 15 August 1948. After war, the Rhee autocracy and military rule under Park and Chun, it industrialised at great speed and became a democracy after 1987, now one of the world's major economies and cultural exporters.
summary.zh: 1948年8月15日在半岛南部建立。经历战争、李承晚的独裁以及朴正熙和全斗焕的军人统治后，韩国高速工业化，1987年后实现民主化，如今是世界主要经济体和文化输出国之一。

sources.title: Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Don Oberdorfer, The Two Koreas: A Contemporary History (Addison-Wesley, 1997)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: South Korea
Wikipedia: South Korea

name.zh: 朝鲜民主主义人民共和国

summary.en: Proclaimed in Pyongyang on 9 September 1948 under Kim Il-sung. A one-party state ruled by three generations of the Kim family, it invaded the South in 1950, suffered famine in the 1990s and developed nuclear weapons, testing them from 2006.
summary.zh: 1948年9月9日在平壤宣布成立，由金日成领导。这是一个由金氏家族三代统治的一党制国家，1950年进攻南方，1990年代经历饥荒，并发展核武器，自2006年起进行核试验。

sources.title: Charles K. Armstrong, The North Korean Revolution, 1945–1950 (2003)
Don Oberdorfer, The Two Koreas: A Contemporary History (Addison-Wesley, 1997)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: North Korea
Wikipedia: North Korea
